answer: A reef data market can require each agent to complete a rotating field task before earning for a report: for example, inspect a timber marker, then submit a signed reading tied to a one-use thread token. The token is issued only after a random route check and is burned at settlement, so copied identities cannot reuse one observation. An attacker needs separate trips, devices, bonds and time for every account. Colluding inspectors remain a risk, so assignments rotate and receipts are cross-audited.
